rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own home (hardwood floor, drywall, contents) caused by a burst supply line in their own plumbing is a straightforward property damage claim.
claim_summary: Policyholder Sam Patel (POL-1004) returned from a work trip to find basement flooded with approximately two inches of water caused by a burst supply line under the upstairs bathroom sink that ran for approximately two days. Damage includes buckled hardwood flooring, water-soaked drywall (up to one foot height), and ruined stored items. Estimated damage $8,000–$15,000. $500 deductible applies.

case_facts.description: Two inches of water across entire basement; hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked to approximately one foot height, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.cause: burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink, ran for approximately two days
case_facts.estimated_damage: $8,000–$15,000 (hardwood flooring, drywall, water damage mitigation, ruined contents)

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof structure (shingles on back porch overhang) with no third-party involvement or theft is straightforward property_damage.
claim_summary: Homeowner reports wind damage to back porch roof overhang, with approximately four shingles blown off last weekend. Estimated repair cost $400 with no water intrusion or secondary damage. Claim is below the $2,500 deductible but should be routed for adjuster review to confirm damage assessment and coverage applicability.

case_facts.description: Wind blew approximately four shingles off the overhang above back porch
